note: 12 synthetic abstracts, 3 latent themes by design: docs 0-3 title/abstract screening, docs 4-7 search and query tooling, docs 8-11 structured data extraction and charting.
documents: A language model screened titles and abstracts against the review criteria and reached recall above 0.95 while cutting reviewer screening workload by half.
We compare active-learning screening classifiers that rank records by predicted relevance so reviewers can stop screening once a recall target is reached.
Inter-rater reliability between a model screener and a human screener was measured with Cohen's kappa on the title and abstract screening decisions of three reviews.
A calibration study of confidence scores from a title and abstract screening model, showing that low-confidence records account for most missed includes.
A large language model expands a seed search query with synonyms and MeSH terms, improving the recall of a gold-standard reference set at a small precision cost.
We automatically translate a single Boolean search strategy into the database-specific query syntax of PubMed, Scopus, and Embase.
Backward and forward citation searching tools were benchmarked for their ability to find studies that the Boolean database search had missed.
A federated search client sends one query to several bibliographic database APIs in parallel and merges the heterogeneous search results into one record list.
A structured data extraction pipeline reads trial reports and returns the population, intervention, and outcome fields, each with a verbatim supporting quote.
We compare form-based data charting templates for scoping reviews and measure how often two extractors record the same charted value for each field.
An automated charting tool links every extracted data item back to the exact sentence in the source document that the value was taken from.
Field-level accuracy of automated data extraction from methods sections was measured against a double-extracted reference standard for each data item.
